title: PROVISIONAL ESTIMATES OF SERVICE PRODUCER PRICE INDICES (BASE YEAR 2022-23)  FOR Q1 OF FY 2026-27 AND FINAL INDICES FOR Q4 OF FY 2025-26
body_text:

Note: Weights have not been assigned to aforementioned services as these services do not cover the entire service sector. However, sub-service level weights under each service, have been computed using the data of FY 2022-23 for arriving at the PPI of respective Services.
The Service Producer Price Indices (Base Year 2022-23) and the Year-on-Year (YoY) inflation rate of the seven services for last four quarters are given at Annexure . Quarterly Service PPIs from Q1 of FY 2023-24 to Q1 of FY 2026-27 are available at ( https://eaindustry.nic.in/download_data_2223.asp )
Service PPIs for seven services for Q2 of FY 2026-27 will be released on Wednesday, 25 th November 2026.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Commerce & Industry released provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for Q1 FY 2026-27 and final indices for Q4 FY 2025-26, covering seven services: securities transactions, banking, pension fund management, insurance, telecom, railways, and air passenger services (Base Year 2022-23). Notable movements include a sharp rise in the Air (Passenger) Service Price Index to 126.4 (31.94% YoY inflation) and an increase in the Pension Fund Management index to 113.3 (5.2% YoY). The next release, covering Q2 FY 2026-27, is scheduled for 25 November 2026.
enrichment.context: Producer Price Indices for services measure the change in prices received by producers for services rendered, complementing the Consumer Price Index and Wholesale Price Index frameworks used to track inflation and output pricing in the economy. India has been progressively developing Service PPIs since services contribute over 50% of GDP, yet historically lacked robust price measurement compared to goods (WPI) and retail prices (CPI). The base year 2022-23 series is part of ongoing statistical modernization efforts by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry (through the Office of Economic Adviser) to improve macroeconomic data granularity, which feeds into GDP deflators, inflation targeting by the RBI, and sector-specific policy analysis. This is a routine, recurring quarterly statistical release rather than a new policy or landmark data initiative, and it currently covers only seven select services rather than the entire service sector.
